segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have a lesson that comes actually from a user request.
segments.zh: 我是凯瑟琳，今天我们这一课其实来自一位用户的请求。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We had a user request who asked us if we can do something about a purchasing manager, maybe what his job does or what it is to be a purchasing manager.
segments.zh: 有位用户来信问，能不能讲讲采购经理，比如他的工作内容，或者当采购经理到底是怎么一回事。

segments.en: So you'll find out all about that today in this lesson.
segments.zh: 因此，您今天将在本课中找到有关这一切的信息。

segments.en: It's an upper intermediate about being a purchasing manager and about vendors.
segments.zh: 这是一期中高级课程，讲的是当采购经理和供应商的事。

segments.en: So let's check out today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以让我们看看今天的对话。

segments.en: Good morning, Angela.
segments.zh: 早上好，安吉拉。

segments.en: How have you been lately?
segments.zh: 你最近过得怎么样？

segments.en: Morning Michael.
segments.zh: 早上好，迈克尔。

segments.en: I've been very busy lately.
segments.zh: 我最近很忙。

segments.en: One of our other vendors is going out of business and I've been searching for a suitable replacement.
segments.zh: 我们另一家供应商快要倒闭了，我最近一直在找合适的替代供应商。

segments.en: Well rest assured that you can count on us to be here for the long run.
segments.zh: 请放心，您可以指望我们长期在这里。

segments.en: Please sit down.
segments.zh: 请坐下。

segments.en: Coffee?
segments.zh: 咖啡？

segments.en: No thanks.
segments.zh: 不用了，谢谢。

segments.en: I've been trying to cut down on the caffeine.
segments.zh: 我一直在努力减少咖啡因。

segments.en: I could never do that.
segments.zh: 我永远做不到。

segments.en: I'd be a zombie if I didn't have my morning coffee fix.
segments.zh: 早上要是不喝杯咖啡提神，我就跟行尸走肉一样。

segments.en: Let's get down to business then.
segments.zh: 那我们来谈正事吧。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I've come to talk with you about ordering the 8 megapixel cameras for our new MiPhone.
segments.zh: 我这次来，是想谈谈为我们的新款 MiPhone 订购八百万像素摄像头的事。

segments.en: The demand for phone cameras is growing and Pear has been falling behind in the market.
segments.zh: 手机摄像头的需求不断增长，而 Pear 在市场上已经落后了。

segments.en: That's great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: I'm glad to hear that Pear has finally jumped on the bandwagon.
segments.zh: 我很高兴听到 Pear 终于加入了潮流。

segments.en: Right now our contract is for the 5 megapixel cameras.
segments.zh: 我们目前签的合同是五百万像素摄像头。

segments.en: Is Pear still interested in having those?
segments.zh: Pear 还打算要这款吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: We're changing all the cameras to 8 megapixels.
segments.zh: 我们要把摄像头全部改成八百万像素。

segments.en: We were hoping that by making your company our sole supplier for cameras, we could negotiate a better deal.
segments.zh: 我们希望，把贵公司作为我们唯一的摄像头供应商，能谈成更划算的条件。

segments.en: Surely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: Let's get started by drafting a new contract.
segments.zh: 让我们开始起草一份新合同。

segments.en: Alright we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So a very interesting job to be a purchasing manager.
segments.zh: 所以，当采购经理是份很有意思的工作。

segments.en: A lot of responsibility on top of him.
segments.zh: 他肩上的责任很重。

segments.en: And we actually saw some really interesting phrases and words that are related to business, to negotiating, contracts, etc.
segments.zh: 我们实际上看到了一些与业务相关的非常有趣的短语和单词，与谈判、合同等有关。

segments.en: So let's take a look at some of those now on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们来语言要点里看看其中一些。

segments.en: The first word we have is vendor.
segments.zh: 我们的第一个词是供应商。

segments.en: This is a noun.
segments.zh: 这是一个名词。

segments.en: It means it's a job.
segments.zh: 这意味着这是一份工作。

segments.en: It's the name of a person's job.
segments.zh: 这是一个人的工作名称。

segments.en: So he is a vendor.
segments.zh: 所以他是一个供应商。

segments.en: And a vendor, what does a vendor do?
segments.zh: 和供应商，供应商是做什么的？

segments.en: Well, a vendor sells things.
segments.zh: 好吧，卖家卖东西。

segments.en: So the verb here is to vend, like a vending machine is that machine that you can buy sodas from.
segments.zh: 所以这里的动词是贩卖，就像自动售货机是你可以从中购买苏打水的机器。

segments.en: So a vendor is someone who sells things to someone else.
segments.zh: 所以供应商是向别人出售东西的人。

segments.en: Okay so I can say he is a door vendor.
segments.zh: 好吧，我可以说他是个卖门的供应商。

segments.en: He sells doors?
segments.zh: 他卖门？

segments.en: Yeah, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: Or let me contact my vendor about the price list for these TVs.
segments.zh: 或者让我联系我的供应商了解这些电视的价格表。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So we're talking about a vendor who is going out of business.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈论的是一个倒闭的供应商。

segments.en: And because he's going out of business, this manager is actually looking for a suitable replacement.
segments.zh: 而且因为他要倒闭了，这位经理实际上是在寻找合适的替代者。

segments.en: So this is an interesting phrase because these two words normally go together.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的短语，因为这两个词通常并存。

segments.en: We say let's find a replacement, okay that's good, but really we want a suitable replacement.
segments.zh: 我们说让我们找到一个替代品，好吧，这很好，但我们真的想要一个合适的替代品。

segments.en: And so first of all, the word suitable means like appropriate or good.
segments.zh: 所以首先，这个词的意思是合适的或好的。

segments.en: But what about replacement?
segments.zh: 但是更换呢？

segments.en: What does this mean?
segments.zh: 这是什么意思？

segments.en: A replacement is something that takes the place of.
segments.zh: 替代品是取代的东西。

segments.en: It replaces something else.
segments.zh: 它取代了其他东西。

segments.en: So for example, we have our vendor who went out of business.
segments.zh: 例如，我们的供应商倒闭了。

segments.en: So what we are looking now for is another vendor, but not just any vendor, a suitable vendor, one that has the things that we need or the prices that we need.
segments.zh: 所以我们现在正在寻找的是另一个供应商，但不仅仅是任何供应商，合适的供应商，拥有我们需要的东西或我们需要的价格的供应商。

segments.en: And in order to replace the one that went out of business.
segments.zh: 而且是为了取代那家倒闭的供应商。

segments.en: Right, so we can say this about other things, not just people.
segments.zh: 对，所以我们可以说其他事情，而不仅仅是人。

segments.en: For example, if I break my iPhone, my cell phone, very expensive phone, I'm upset about it.
segments.zh: 例如，如果我弄坏了我的 iPhone、我的手机、非常昂贵的手机，我会对此感到不安。

segments.en: But when I buy a new one, I don't want a cheap one.
segments.zh: 但买新的时，我不想要便宜的。

segments.en: I want a suitable replacement, one that's about the same as the old one.
segments.zh: 我想要一个合适的替代品，一个和旧的差不多。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So maybe you don't get the exact same one, but you get one that's very similar.
segments.zh: 所以也许你没有得到完全相同的一个，但你得到了一个非常相似的东西。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So now they're going to talk a little bit about the contract, but they kind of do a little bit of small talk and they're talking about coffee and he says, well, you know, I'd be a zombie if I didn't have my morning coffee fix.
segments.zh: 所以现在他们要谈谈合同，但他们有点闲聊，他们在谈论咖啡，他说，好吧，你知道，如果我没有早上喝咖啡，我会成为一个僵尸。

segments.en: I know how that feels.
segments.zh: 我知道那是什么感觉。

segments.en: This is a person who loves to drink caffeine to wake up.
segments.zh: 这个人喜欢靠摄入咖啡因来提神。

segments.en: And so we talk about a fix as being something that you need.
segments.zh: 所以我们把 fix 说成是你离不开的东西。

segments.en: Okay, my coffee fix means the coffee that I drink in the morning to survive.
segments.zh: 好，my coffee fix 指的就是我早上不喝就没法活的咖啡。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, so we know the verb to fix is to make something good again, to repair.
segments.zh: 好，我们知道动词 fix 的意思是让东西重新变好，也就是修理。

segments.en: But in this case, we're taking fix as a noun and we're saying that it's something that you need, like you said, for example, maybe in the morning you need your English fix and so you'd listen to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，我们将 fix 作为名词，我们说这是您需要的东西，例如，就像您所说的那样，也许在早上您需要您的英语 fix，所以您会听 EnglishPod。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: You need it so much, it's like a drug.
segments.zh: 你非常需要它，它就像一种药物。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And moving on, they started to talk a little bit more about the details of the business and he mentioned that they want to make this company their sole supplier for cameras.
segments.zh: 继续，他们开始更多地谈论业务细节，他提到他们希望让这家公司成为他们唯一的相机供应商。

segments.en: Okay, so sole means only.
segments.zh: 好的，sole 的意思是唯一的。

segments.en: But this word supplier is very interesting because it's very similar to vendor.
segments.zh: 但是这个词供应商非常有趣，因为它与供应商非常相似。

segments.en: So it's basically someone, a company maybe, or a person that supplies you with what you need.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上是某人，一个公司，或者一个为你提供你需要的东西的人。

segments.en: All right, so to supply is to provide for.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以供应就是提供。

segments.en: So for example, if I work at a clothing store and I sell lots of nice clothing, I need a supplier to bring me the clothes that I sell.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，如果我在一家服装店工作并且出售了很多漂亮的服装，我需要一个供应商来给我带来我出售的衣服。

segments.en: Otherwise, where am I going to get them from?
segments.zh: 否则，我要从哪里得到它们？

segments.en: I don't have a factory.
segments.zh: 我没有工厂。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: For example, IBM is one of the biggest computer suppliers or manufacturers in the world.
segments.zh: 例如，IBM 是世界上最大的计算机供应商或制造商之一。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And for the last part of the dialogue, they said, well, I think we can reach an agreement.
segments.zh: 在对话的最后一部分，他们说：嗯，我想我们可以达成协议。

segments.en: Let's get started by drafting a new contract.
segments.zh: 让我们开始起草一份新合同。

segments.en: They're going to draft a contract.
segments.zh: 他们将起草一份合同。

segments.en: All right, so this is interesting because we don't use the verb to write a contract.
segments.zh: 好，这很有意思，因为我们不说 write a contract。

segments.en: Now you would think, well, of course you write it, but there's a special verb that we use with the word contract.
segments.zh: 你可能会想，合同当然是写出来的，但 contract 这个词有一个专门的动词搭配。

segments.en: So just remember this phrase together, to draft a contract or my company will draft a contract and send it to you.
segments.zh: 所以把这一整句一起记住：draft a contract，比如说，我们公司会起草一份合同发给你。

segments.en: This means to prepare a contract in order for someone to sign it.
segments.zh: 这意味着准备一份合同，以便某人签署合同。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's basically the same as write, but it's usually used more with contracts to draft a contract.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上和 write 一样，但更多用在合同上，比如 draft a contract。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Or maybe you can say to draft up a business plan.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说起草商业计划。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So to draft a plan, to draft a contract.
segments.zh: 所以要起草一个计划，起草一份合同。

segments.en: This is basically to write something that has many different points, many different strategies.
segments.zh: 这基本上是写一些有许多不同点、许多不同策略的东西。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So five key words for you there.
segments.zh: 所以那里有五个关键词要讲。

segments.en: And now let's move on to some key phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 现在让我们继续讨论流利表达的一些关键短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay, so there are a lot of really, really juicy phrases in today's lesson.
segments.zh: 好的，所以今天的课程中有很多非常非常有趣的短语。

segments.en: The first one is rest assured.
segments.zh: 第一个是放心。

segments.en: So we heard this from Michael at the beginning of the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我们在对话开始时从迈克尔那里听到了这一点。

segments.en: He said, rest assured that you can count on us.
segments.zh: 他说，请放心，你可以指望我们。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Rest assured.
segments.zh: 放心。

segments.en: So this is a phrase that you use to try to give confidence to someone, telling them you can trust me, rest assured that I'll be there.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个短语，你用来试图给某人信心，告诉他们你可以相信我，请放心，我会在那里。

segments.en: Don't worry.
segments.zh: 别担心。

segments.en: Don't worry.
segments.zh: 别担心。

segments.en: So let's hear another example of it.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听另一个例子。

segments.en: Rest assured, Marco, I will be there to support you.
segments.zh: 放心，马可，我会在那里支持你。

segments.en: Okay, so I know that you will be there or I can trust that you'll be there.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我知道你会在那里，或者我可以相信你会在那里。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So to rest assure.
segments.zh: 所以要放心。

segments.en: Now the second part of it is in that same sentence, well, rest assure that you can count on us.
segments.zh: 现在它的第二部分在同一句话中，好吧，请放心，你可以依靠我们。

segments.en: Okay, so what does it mean to count on us, to count on me?
segments.zh: 好吧，指望我们，指望我是什么意思？

segments.en: So the verb to count has a couple of different meanings and most of us are familiar with the other one, to count numbers, one, two, three, four, five.
segments.zh: 所以动词 to count 有几个不同的含义，我们大多数人都熟悉另一种，来计算数字，一、二、三、四、五。

segments.en: But here to count on someone, remember that preposition on, means to expect someone to do something, to depend on someone.
segments.zh: 但在这里指望某人，记住这个介词，意味着期望某人做某事，依赖某人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if you count on someone, means that you depend on them, you rely on them, you can trust them.
segments.zh: 所以如果你指望某人，意味着你依赖他们，你依赖他们，你可以信任他们。

segments.en: So for example, in the sentence that I just told Marco, rest assured, I will be there.
segments.zh: 例如，在我刚刚告诉 Marco 的句子中，请放心，我会在那里。

segments.en: You can count on me.
segments.zh: 你可以指望我。

segments.en: That means you can depend on me, you can expect me to be there.
segments.zh: 这意味着你可以依靠我，你可以期待我在那里。

segments.en: I will not let you down.
segments.zh: 我不会让你失望的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: In that same sentence, we have another phrasal verb, rest assured that you can count on us to be here for the long run.
segments.zh: 在同一句话中，我们有另一个短语动词，请放心，您可以指望我们长期在这里。

segments.en: The long run.
segments.zh: 长期来看。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we're not actually running here.
segments.zh: 所以我们实际上并没有在这里运行。

segments.en: The long run is a phrase that means for a long time.
segments.zh: the long run 这个短语的意思是长期。

segments.en: So for example, if I'm in an interview and someone asks me, well, we're really interested in your resume and we really like you.
segments.zh: 例如，如果我在面试中有人问我，那么，我们对你的简历很感兴趣，我们真的很喜欢你。

segments.en: We want to know, are you available in the long run, in the long term?
segments.zh: 我们想知道，从长远看，你能长期做下去吗？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if you say, yes, I am here for the long run, it means that you are here for a long time.
segments.zh: 所以如果你说：是的，我会长期待在这里，意思就是你会待很长时间。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And let's move on to our next phrase.
segments.zh: 让我们继续我们的下一个短语。

segments.en: And they're actually, you know, they stopped with a small talk and now they want to get down to business.
segments.zh: 其实，你知道，他们结束了闲聊，现在想谈正事了。

segments.en: You hear this phrase all the time because you don't just walk into a meeting and start talking about business stuff.
segments.zh: 您一直听到这句话，因为您不只是走进会议并开始谈论商业内容。

segments.en: You know, you start with the nice things first.
segments.zh: 你知道，先聊些轻松愉快的东西。

segments.en: You say, how was your weekend?
segments.zh: 你说，你的周末过得怎么样？

segments.en: How is your wife?
segments.zh: 你老婆怎么样？

segments.en: How was that game of golf?
segments.zh: 那场高尔夫球比赛怎么样？

segments.en: So you're talking about nice small talk, like you just said, Marco, but when you want to start talking about numbers or products, things like that, that is called business.
segments.zh: 所以你说的是不错的闲聊，就像你刚才说的那样，马可，但是当你想开始谈论数字或产品时，诸如此类的事情，就是所谓的商业。

segments.en: So when you want to start that, you say, let's get down to business.
segments.zh: 所以当你想开始时，你说，我们来谈正事吧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's a phrase to say, okay, now let's start talking about what we came here to do.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个短语，好吧，现在让我们开始谈谈我们来这里做什么。

segments.en: Start talking about business.
segments.zh: 开始谈论商业。

segments.en: And the last phrase that we have for you, it's a very interesting phrase.
segments.zh: 我们为您准备的最后一句话，这是一个非常有趣的短语。

segments.en: When they were talking about one of the brands of phones, they're saying, I'm glad to hear that Pear has finally jumped on the bandwagon.
segments.zh: 当他们谈论手机品牌之一时，他们说，我很高兴听到 Pear 终于加入了潮流。

segments.en: Now, Marco, I wish I could tell you, I knew where this phrase came from, but I don't.
segments.zh: 现在，马可，我希望我能告诉你，我知道这句话是从哪里来的，但我不知道。

segments.en: Let's just talk about the word bandwagon first.
segments.zh: 我们先来说说 bandwagon 这个词。

segments.en: I think bandwagon means something that everyone is doing.
segments.zh: 我觉得 bandwagon 指的是大家都在做的事。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I think if everyone likes the color purple and all of a sudden you like the color purple, then that means you just jumped on the bandwagon.
segments.zh: 所以我想如果每个人都喜欢紫色，突然间你喜欢紫色，那就意味着你只是赶上了潮流。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I jumped on the bandwagon.
segments.zh: 我也随大流了。

segments.en: So you think of a wagon as like, before they had cars, they had wagons.
segments.zh: 所以你就把 wagon 想象成马车，在有汽车之前，人们坐的是马车。

segments.en: They're wooden and they have wheels and they're pulled by a horse.
segments.zh: 它们是木制的，它们有轮子，它们被马拉着。

segments.en: And so everyone is on there and they're all going somewhere.
segments.zh: 大家都在车上，一起去某个地方。

segments.en: And I wasn't on it, but I jumped on the back.
segments.zh: 我原本不在车上，但我从后面跳了上去。

segments.en: That means I joined everyone.
segments.zh: 这意味着我加入了所有人。

segments.en: I started to do what they're doing.
segments.zh: 我开始做他们正在做的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I guess you agree with them or you're going towards in the same direction that everyone else is going.
segments.zh: 所以我猜你同意他们的观点，或者你正朝着其他人的方向前进。

segments.en: Look at Marco.
segments.zh: 看看马可。

segments.en: He just bought an iPhone.
segments.zh: 他刚买了一部iPhone。

segments.en: Now he's jumped on the bandwagon.
segments.zh: 现在他赶上了潮流。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So everyone is going in the same direction.
segments.zh: 所以每个人都朝着同一个方向前进。

segments.en: Everyone is doing the same thing.
segments.zh: 每个人都在做同样的事情。

segments.en: Everyone likes the same thing.
segments.zh: 每个人都喜欢同样的事情。

segments.en: So to jump on the bandwagon, you can use it in the business sense.
segments.zh: 所以 jump on the bandwagon 这个说法，也可以用在商业场合。

segments.en: For example, if somebody is not agreeing with you or somebody doesn't want to support your project, you can say, I would really appreciate it if you jumped on the bandwagon and supported us on this.
segments.zh: 例如，如果有人不同意你，或者不愿意支持你的项目，你可以说：如果你能加入进来支持我们这件事，我会非常感激。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's not always a bad thing, but remember that the verb that is synonymous with this is to conform.
segments.zh: 所以这并不总是一件坏事，但请记住，与此同义的动词是顺从。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: To do what everyone else is doing.
segments.zh: 做其他人正在做的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting things here.
segments.zh: 这里有很多有趣的事情。

segments.en: Let's listen to our dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 我们最后再听一遍对话。

segments.en: Good morning, Angela.
segments.zh: 早上好，安吉拉。

segments.en: How have you been lately?
segments.zh: 你最近过得怎么样？

segments.en: Morning Michael.
segments.zh: 早上迈克尔。

segments.en: I've been very busy lately.
segments.zh: 我最近很忙。

segments.en: One of our other vendors is going out of business and I've been searching for a suitable replacement.
segments.zh: 我们另一家供应商快要倒闭了，我最近一直在找合适的替代供应商。

segments.en: Well rest assured that you can count on us to be here for the long run.
segments.zh: 请放心，您可以指望我们长期在这里。

segments.en: Please sit down.
segments.zh: 请坐下。

segments.en: Coffee?
segments.zh: 咖啡？

segments.en: No, thanks.
segments.zh: 不，谢谢。

segments.en: I've been trying to cut down on the caffeine.
segments.zh: 我一直在努力减少咖啡因。

segments.en: I could never do that.
segments.zh: 我永远做不到。

segments.en: I'd be a zombie if I didn't have my morning coffee fix.
segments.zh: 早上要是不喝杯咖啡提神，我就跟行尸走肉一样。

segments.en: Let's get down to business then.
segments.zh: 那我们来谈正事吧。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I've come to talk with you about ordering the eight megapixel cameras for our new Mi phone.
segments.zh: 我来和你谈谈为我们的新 Mi 手机订购八百万像素摄像头的事。

segments.en: The demand for phone cameras is growing and Pear has been falling behind in the market.
segments.zh: 手机摄像头的需求不断增长，而 Pear 在市场上已经落后了。

segments.en: That's great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: I'm glad to hear that Pear has finally jumped on the bandwagon.
segments.zh: 我很高兴听到 Pear 终于加入了潮流。

segments.en: Right now our contract is for the five megapixel cameras.
segments.zh: 目前我们的合同是五百万像素的摄像头。

segments.en: Is Pear still interested in having those?
segments.zh: Pear 还打算要这款吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: We're changing all the cameras to eight megapixels.
segments.zh: 我们要把所有摄像头都改成八百万像素。

segments.en: We were hoping that by making your company our sole supplier for cameras, we could negotiate a better deal.
segments.zh: 我们希望，把贵公司作为我们唯一的摄像头供应商，能谈成更划算的条件。

segments.en: Surely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: Let's get started by drafting a new contract.
segments.zh: 让我们开始起草一份新合同。

segments.en: So talking about purchasing, it's actually a very interesting position.
segments.zh: 所以说到购买，这实际上是一个非常有趣的位置。

segments.en: I think many, or almost all companies, big companies have this position where not only do they have to, maybe if they're in retailing, they have to purchase the goods that they will sell, but also in offices.
segments.zh: 我觉得很多公司，几乎所有大公司，都有这个职位；如果做零售，他们不仅要采购要卖的商品，办公室里同样也要采购。

segments.en: For example, who buys the paper, the printers, the copiers, everything for the office?
segments.zh: 例如，谁为办公室买纸、打印机、复印机和所有东西？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: This is a very important position, as you say, because this person can save a company a lot of money if the person knows the right vendors.
segments.zh: 正如您所说，这是一个非常重要的职位，因为如果这个人认识合适的供应商，这个人可以为公司节省很多钱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: If the only vendors you know are selling things at very high prices, then that's not very good for you or for your business.
segments.zh: 如果您认识的唯一供应商以非常高的价格出售商品，那么这对您或您的业务都不是很好。

segments.en: But if you know all the inside secrets, you know all the good vendors, then maybe you're going to be able to save a lot of money.
segments.zh: 但如果你知道所有的内部秘密，你就知道所有的好供应商，那么也许你就能省下很多钱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: I think this position is also a lot broader than just this.
segments.zh: 我认为这个职位也远不止于此。

segments.en: Maybe someone can also help us out on the website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 也许有人也可以在网站 englishpod.com 上帮助我们。

segments.en: You can explain.
segments.zh: 你可以解释。

segments.en: Maybe if you're a purchasing manager, you can tell us what your job entails.
segments.zh: 也许如果您是采购经理，您可以告诉我们您的工作需要什么。

segments.en: Or if you know a purchasing manager, what does that person do?
segments.zh: 或者如果你认识一个采购经理，那个人是做什么的？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We're very curious to know, and we hope that you'll be able to use some of these new words and phrases.
segments.zh: 我们很想知道，我们希望您能够使用其中一些新单词和短语。

segments.en: If you want to practice, check us out, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 如果您想练习，请查看我们，Englishpod.com。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
